B3.name: Citizen-led efforts to  counter manipulation & promote content integrity

B7.name: Adjusting government behaviour in the face of AI towards democratic resilience

B1.label: AI literacy
B1.description: Education, training, and awareness programmes that equip citizens and institutions to understand and engage with AI.
B1.name: Civic & AI literacy building

B2.label: Levelling the playing field
B2.description: AI as a tool to promote inclusion, lowering participation barriers and equalising chances of being heard in democratic processes or institutional settings.
B2.name: Levelling the playing field

B3.label: Citizen-led content integrity
B3.description: Downstream tools and systems deployed by citizens, civil society, platforms, or public institutions to protect information integrity.
B3.name: Citizen-led efforts to  counter manipulation & promote content integrity

B3A.label: Deepfake detection & authentication
B3A.description: Downstream tools and systems that detect, authenticate, or counter synthetic and manipulative content deployed by citizens, civil society, platforms, or public institutions after content is generated.
B3A.name: Citizen-led efforts to  counter manipulation & promote content integrity

B3B.label: Verified information
B3B.description: Systems that proactively provide verified, trustworthy information to citizens to counter misinformation by offering reliable alternatives.
B3B.name: Citizen-led efforts to  counter manipulation & promote content integrity

B4.label: Participation infrastructure
B4.description: AI that powers the vehicles through which citizen deliberation and democratic participation take place (moderation, summarisation, new participatory formats, etc.).
B4.name: Infrastructure for citizen participation

B4A.label: Discourse moderation
B4A.description: AI that sorts, orders, and moderates content within deliberative processes without altering or summarising it.
B4A.name: Infrastructure for citizen participation

B4B.label: Synthesising public input
B4B.description: AI that transforms deliberative content, making the substance of a discussion more accessible to both governments and other participants.
B4B.name: Infrastructure for citizen participation

B4C.label: Participatory formats
B4C.description: Developing new deliberative formats and participatory spaces enabled by AI and innovations to the architectures of participation.
B4C.name: Infrastructure for citizen participation

B5.label: Cyber defence
B5.description: Tools that protect digital and physical infrastructure against AI-powered cyber threats.
B5.name: Defensive cybersecurity resilience

B6.label: Legal accountability frameworks
B6.description: Hard law that creates enforceable accountability for AI harms (liability rules, regulatory requirements, and oversight mechanisms backed by enforceable sanctions).
B6.name: Legal & accountability frameworks

B6A.label: Operational requirements
B6A.description: Rules that mandate specific actions, standards, or procedures for AI systems (labelling obligations, disclosure formats, human-in-the-loop requirements, decision-record mandates, bias testing protocols, and other prescriptive operating conditions imposed by regulators).
B6A.name: Legal & accountability frameworks

B6B.label: Prohibitions & restrictions
B6B.description: Laws that ban or limit specific uses of AI (prohibitions on deceptive election content, robocall restrictions, data privacy protections, content restrictions, sanctions on entities enabling AI-facilitated harms, …).
B6B.name: Legal & accountability frameworks

B6C.label: Liability & enforcement
B6C.description: Legal rules that create consequences for AI-related harms after they occur (liability frameworks, duty of care requirements, mandatory audits, independent oversight mandates, enforceable remedies, …).
B6C.name: Legal & accountability frameworks

B6D.label: Market-shaping rules
B6D.description: Regulations that reshape the competitive landscape to prevent concentration and lock-in (interoperability mandates, multi-provider requirements, data portability obligations, procurement conditions, …) .
B6D.name: Legal & accountability frameworks

B7.label: Government adapting to AI
B7.description: Actions taken by state actors (executive, legislative, judicial, administrative, electoral bodies at any level) to keep core governance functions operating effectively under AI-induced pressure.
B7.name: Adjusting government behaviour in the face of AI towards democratic resilience

B7A.label: Government AI capacity
B7A.description: Training, hiring, funding, and organising the people and structures state bodies need to operate in an AI context.
B7A.name: Adjusting government behaviour in the face of AI towards democratic resilience

B7B.label: Guardrails on government AI
B7B.description: Technical requirements and infrastructure that state bodies impose on AI systems they themselves deploy.
B7B.name: Adjusting government behaviour in the face of AI towards democratic resilience

B7C.label: Resilience without AI
B7C.description: Changes to core government and institutional processes (not involving AI deployment) that harden democratic functions against AI-enabled pressures.
B7C.name: Adjusting government behaviour in the face of AI towards democratic resilience

B7D.label: Resilience through AI
B7D.description: Government adoption of AI specifically to strengthen democratic functions under AI-induced pressure.
B7D.name: Adjusting government behaviour in the face of AI towards democratic resilience

B9.label: Democratic oversight of AI
B9.description: Processes through which citizens and civil society organisations shape how AI is designed, deployed, and governed.
B9.name: Democratic oversight of AI

B10.label: Responsible AI development
B10.description: Design, training, and deployment choices by AI developers that shape democratic outcomes – training models for truthfulness and autonomy, content filtering, hallucination prevention, and safety engineering.
B10.name: Responsible AI development practices

B10A.label: Democratic value alignment
B10A.description: Developer choices about model character at training time, pre- and post-training (training for truthfulness, epistemic health, user autonomy, pro-social behaviour, …).
B10A.name: Responsible AI development practices

B10B.label: Safety by design
B10B.description: Developer-side technical measures that reduce harm after training (red-teaming, content filtering, input/output guardrails, …).
B10B.name: Responsible AI development practices

B11.label: Building the evidence base
B11.description: Research, metrics, evaluation frameworks, monitoring systems, audits, multi-agent simulations, and scientific evidence bases that inform AI governance decisions that build the epistemic foundations needed to act.
B11.name: Establishing knowledge & evidence infrastructure

B11A.label: Model evaluations
B11A.description: Research and technical evidence base about AI models themselves (capability thresholds, institutional safety levels – ISLs, benchmarks, evaluation methodologies, etc.). Focused on measuring what models can do.
B11A.name: Establishing knowledge & evidence infrastructure

B11B.label: Deployment monitoring
B11B.description: Observation, collecting empirical evidence, and forecasting, focusing on tracking the effects of AI and mapping where risks emerge.
B11B.name: Establishing knowledge & evidence infrastructure

B11C.label: Research synthesis & coordination
B11C.description: Conceptual, methodological, and synthesising work that equips actors to make sense of AI and its governance.
B11C.name: Establishing knowledge & evidence infrastructure
